text.p: Imaging Diagnostic Systems Inc said Tuesday that it will withhold conversion rights on its Series B and C convertible preferred shares until it can ascertain what caused the recent decline in the price of its stock.

In a statement, the medical technology company said it is looking at whether the recent unusual market activity in its stock was related to its March 25 amendment of a registration statement for common shares intended to be issued on conversion of the preferred stock.

In February, the company filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission's for up to 2.0 million common shares that would be issued on conversion of its Series B preferred stock. In the amendment, it included Series C preferred as eligible for conversion and raised the number of common shares issuable to 4.27 million.
"Our stock has lost 40-50 percent of its value since March 20 and it has continued to go down," said the company's general counsel and vice-president, Peter Knezevich.
He declined to elaborate, but said that the amended filing was still pending with the SEC.
Imaging Diagnostic traded at 2-9/16, down 1/8, in late afternoon trading.
